summary: Completed the initial scenario-complete review of Canadian Solar Inc. after its 2026-07-31 bullish-MACD crossover. Q1 2026 storage shipments rose 142% year on year, but module shipments fell 64%, revenue fell 10%, reported gross margin included a USD 93 million tariff refund, operating cash flow was negative USD 209 million, and total debt reached USD 6.8 billion. A conservative attributable-book NAV gives USD 10.43/18.78/27.12 bear/base/bull values, USD 17.943 probability-weighted fair value, 18.9854117425640888123036307% expected return, 14.23905880692306660922772302% confidence-adjusted expected return, and a USD 15.024 buy-below price versus the USD 15.079999923706055 mark. The deterministic research rating is Buy/Initiate, but the security remains watch-tier and allocation-ineligible because both downside-payoff gates fail and relationship status is pending. No conviction strategy or idea follow-up was created.

evidence.claim: Canadian Solar reported Q1 2026 module shipments of 2.5 GW, down 64% year on year, and storage shipments of 2.1 GWh, up 142%. Net revenue fell 10% to USD 1.078 billion. Reported gross margin was 25.1% but included a USD 93 million tariff-refund benefit; Q2 gross-margin guidance was 13-15%. Net loss attributable to shareholders was USD 32 million, operating cash flow was negative USD 209 million, cash was USD 1.441 billion, and total debt including financing liabilities was USD 6.8 billion at March 31, 2026.

Canadian Solar's audited 2025 Form 20-F identifies 67,816,724 common shares outstanding at January 31, 2026 and documents module and storage manufacturing, Recurrent Energy project assets, subsidiary and minority interests, trade-policy exposure, project-sale execution, financing needs and cyclical pricing risks used in the NAV assessment.

Canadian Solar's July 23, 2026 Form 6-K discloses a EUR 50 million Green Medium Term Note Program for solar and storage projects and general corporate purposes, backed by a parent guarantee capped at EUR 65 million. It adds bounded funding capacity while reinforcing financing and project-execution dependence.
